item.title: Why Java String hashCode() Uses Prime Multiplier 31: Performance and Distribution
item.description:
“Why Java String hashCode() Uses Prime Multiplier 31: Performance and Distribution”

Why does the widely adopted String.hashCode() implementation in Java consistently leverage the specific odd prime number 31 as its multiplier? This decision, rooted in performance gains and distribution quality, deserves detailed examination. The rationale stems from a blend of historical precedent, algebraic properties, and empirical testing related to hash table efficiency.

Performance Optimization: The Algebraic Trick

A major driver for selecting 31 is its mathematical relationship to powers of two, making multiplication exceptionally fast on many processor architectures.
